title: "Files & Data Manipulation"

## Reading and Writing Files

### Text Files

```{julia}
# Writing to a file
open("example.txt", "w") do f
    write(f, "Hello, Julia!")
end

# Reading from a file
content = read("example.txt", String)
println(content)
```

### CSV Files

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using CSV, DataFrames

# Read CSV
df = CSV.read("data.csv", DataFrame)

# Write CSV
CSV.write("output.csv", df)
```

## DataFrames

DataFrames are tabular data structures similar to pandas in Python or data.frames in R.

### Creating DataFrames

```{julia}
using DataFrames

# Create from columns
df = DataFrame(
    name = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"],
    age = [25, 30, 35],
    city = ["Helsinki", "Espoo", "Tampere"]
)
```

### Basic Operations

```{julia}
# Select columns
df[:, :name]
```

```{julia}
# Filter rows
filter(row -> row.age > 25, df)
```

```{julia}
# Add new column
df.country = ["Finland", "Finland", "Finland"]
df
```

### Grouping and Aggregation

```{julia}
using Statistics

# Group by and summarize
gdf = groupby(df, :country)
combine(gdf, :age => mean => :avg_age)
```

## Working with Geoscientific Data

### Loading Geophysical Data

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using DelimitedFiles

# Read space-delimited data
data = readdlm("gravity_data.txt")

# Extract columns
x, y, gz = data[:, 1], data[:, 2], data[:, 3]
```

### NetCDF Files

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using NCDatasets

# Read NetCDF
ds = Dataset("climate_data.nc")
temp = ds["temperature"][:]
close(ds)
```
